notes: Each prompt is an INLINE Q&A that forbids plan-mode/tools so the harness can grade the classification the skill teaches: a recurring correction → the RIGHT Claude Code hook EVENT + matcher + warn-vs-block action + a correct settings.json hook JSON shape, with the Claude-only caveat and a confirm-before-write step. The discriminating signal vs a naive (no-skill) answer: naive answers tend to put a 'don't run X command' rule on the wrong event or in memory/CLAUDE.md instead of a PreToolUse Bash matcher; choose 'block' where a cheap 'warn' (PostToolUse) is correct, or vice-versa; conflate a 'don't finish before Y' rule (Stop hook) with a PreToolUse tool gate; mis-place systemMessage/additionalContext against the hookSpecificOutput contract; silently write settings.json without confirmation; and forget that hooks are Claude-Code-only and won't fire for Codex/agy. id 3 explicitly probes the multi-CLI caveat. 2026-07-17 rework (eval-gap-nondiscriminating closure): swapped the two near-duplicate PreToolUse-classification cases for two sharp-edge probes a strong no-skill answer plausibly misses — the fail-open `&& {…} || exit 0` jq lapse (must produce a genuinely fail-closed rewrite) and headless defer-for-external-approval (must answer defer + tool_deferred/-p --resume, not 'ask'). REBALANCED 2026-08-08: a full-panel run showed three of six cases measuring nothing — codex-multi-cli-caveat 10/12 both ways, fail-closed-jq-guard 12/12 both ways, and the protected-path matcher/file_path case ADDED EARLIER THE SAME DAY 11/12 both ways. That last one closed a real coverage gap and still graded nothing: coverage is not discrimination. All three dropped and replaced by two contracts where the intuitive answer is WRONG and the failure is silent — exit 1 does NOT block (only 2 does; anything else is a non-blocking error, so the guard's message appears while the action proceeds), and a resumed `defer` RE-RUNS the hook, so a hook that always defers loops forever instead of replaying the stored approval. The three surviving originals carried the old delta (headless-defer +0.750, changelog-stop-hook +0.333, warn-not-block +0.167).

evals.name: changelog-before-finish-stop-hook
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I keep having to remind you to update CHANGELOG.md before you wrap up a change — you finish without it every time. Make a hook so you can't forget. State exactly which hook EVENT fits, whether it uses a matcher, whether it warns or blocks, and how blocking works for that event.
assertions: Maps 'don't FINISH before doing Y' to a Stop hook (gates completion), NOT a PreToolUse tool gate and not PostToolUse
Notes the Stop event takes NO matcher (unlike tool events)

Chooses to BLOCK completion until the changelog condition holds — via stdout {"decision":"block","reason":"..."} (or exit 2 + stderr) — rather than merely warning, and guards against a Stop loop (e.g. honoring stop_hook_active)
Confirms before writing the hook to settings.json

evals.name: headless pause-for-approval: defer, not ask
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. My automation wrapper launches `claude -p` as a subprocess. When Claude attempts a dangerous Bash command I need the claude PROCESS TO EXIT with that pending tool call preserved, so my wrapper can collect human approval out-of-band (a Slack ping) and later RESUME the same session to have the call re-evaluated. Which hook event and which decision value do I use, what exactly happens at the pause, and how does the resume work? Be precise about any mode restrictions.
assertions: Chooses a PreToolUse hook with permissionDecision "defer" — NOT "ask" (ask prompts interactively and does not exit the process with the call preserved)

States defer is honored only in non-interactive `-p` mode on Claude Code >= v2.1.89 (older versions ignore it and fall through to normal permission handling — worth pinning when an approval gate depends on it), and that it is ignored (with a warning) in interactive sessions and for batched/parallel tool calls

Describes the pause/resume mechanics: the process exits with stop_reason "tool_deferred" and a preserved deferred_tool_use payload; the wrapper resumes via `claude -p --resume <session-id>`, and because the resume just RE-RUNS the hook, the hook must consult the wrapper's persisted decision and return allow/deny (returning defer again re-exits deferred)
Does not attach behavior to fields defer ignores (permissionDecisionReason / updatedInput / additionalContext have no effect on a defer decision)

evals.name: warn-not-block-additionalcontext-vs-systemmessage
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. When I edit files under generated/, I don't want you HARD-BLOCKED — I sometimes legitimately need to — I just want a nudge, aimed at YOU, reminding you the source of truth is elsewhere so you course-correct on your own. Make a hook for that. State the event, whether it can even block, and the exact mechanism you'd use to warn without blocking.
assertions: Recognizes this is a WARN (not block) guardrail and that the natural event (PostToolUse — the edit already happened, or a non-blocking PreToolUse) cannot/should not prevent the action
Warns WITHOUT blocking: exit 0 (not exit 2 / not permissionDecision:deny) so the action proceeds

Uses hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext to steer CLAUDE (the nudge is aimed at the agent to self-correct) — and distinguishes it from systemMessage, which surfaces a note to the USER; picks additionalContext because the user asked for a nudge aimed at the agent — and if it shows systemMessage JSON, places it TOP-LEVEL in the output (never nested inside hookSpecificOutput, where it would be silently ignored)

evals.name: a guard that exits 1 does not guard
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I wrote a PreToolUse hook to stop myself running the full test suite. The script detects the bad command correctly and does `echo 'run only the changed file' >&2; exit 1`. I can see my message in the transcript, but the command still runs every time. Why, and what is the fix?
assertions: Identifies exit code 1 as the cause: only exit 2 is the BLOCKING exit code, and any other non-zero is a NON-blocking error — logged, message surfaced, action allowed to proceed
Gives the fix as `exit 2` (or the equivalent JSON deny decision), not as changing the detection, the matcher, or the message
Explains that seeing the stderr message is consistent with the failure rather than evidence the hook worked — the message being visible is exactly what a non-blocking error does
Does not claim any non-zero exit blocks, and does not suggest exit 1 works on some events

evals.name: a resumed defer re-runs the hook and must not defer again
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I'm building an external approval gate around `claude -p` using a PreToolUse hook that returns permissionDecision `defer`. My wrapper catches the deferred tool call, gets a human approval, and resumes with `--resume <session-id>` — but the run just exits deferred again. What am I missing about what happens on resume?
assertions: Says the resume RE-RUNS the hook rather than replaying the stored decision, so a hook that unconditionally returns defer will defer forever — the loop is the expected consequence, not a bug
Says the hook must consult the wrapper's PERSISTED approval on that second run and return `allow` or `deny` instead of `defer`

Notes at least one real constraint on defer: it is non-interactive `-p` mode only (ignored with a warning in an interactive session), or that it requires a recent enough Claude Code version, or that reason/updatedInput/additionalContext have no effect on a defer
